story_type: moon rocket stages static fired while bolted down, 1965 test film
hook: Seven and a half million pounds of thrust, chained down.
narration: Seven and a half million pounds of thrust, chained to the ground.
This is the first stage of the Saturn V moon rocket, fired in a test stand in 1965.
Five F-1 engines. Full duration tests ran for more than a hundred and fifty seconds.
A static fire straps the stage down, so all that power pushes against the earth instead of lifting off.
In California, the second stage lit its five hydrogen burning J-2 engines at full thrust.
The third stage had a harder job. It would have to restart in space, on the way to the moon.
So engineers fired it, shut it down for an hour and a half, then lit it again.
outcome: In 1965, every stage of the Saturn V passed its static firing.
title: Saturn V stages fired while chained down
description:
A 1966 NASA film shows the static test firings of every Saturn V stage in 1965: five F-1 engines on the first stage in Alabama, the J-2 powered second stage in California, and a stop and restart test of the third stage.

Footage: NASA video (National Archives, Record Group 255), via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Power_for_Apollo_-_Saturn_V.webm
